newsitem.title: USA: Executive says he is not target of grand jury probe.
newsitem.headline: Executive says he is not target of grand jury probe.

text.p: An executive of an Asian-American business group who revealed last month that he was approached by a fund-raiser to funnel money to the Democratic Party said on Monday he has testified before a grand jury and Senate investigators about the incident.

In an interview with local NBC station WRC-TV, Rawlein Soberano, vice president of the Fairfax, Virginia-based Asian-American Business Roundtable, said he had been informed that he was not a target of the grand jury investigation.
Soberano, whose story first appeared in the Washington Post two weeks ago, said John Huang asked him to funnel $300,000 through his association, which would keep $45,000 for its trouble.
Soberano said he refused immediately, something he said caused Huang to "lose face." Huang's reaction was "like a turtle swings back into the shell," he said.
"If I could have swallowed my chicken right there and then, I would have done it, and then got the heck out of there," Soberano said, adding he was "shocked."

Soberano, who sought the meeting with Huang to discuss getting sponsors for his organisation's annual banquet, said he "did not construe it as a front for the DNC (Democratic National Committee)," although he knew Huang was a top DNC fund-raiser.
A Justice Department task force is investigating Huang in connection with possible illegal campaign contributions from foreign sources.
Huang raised about $3.4 million for the Democrats' 1996 campaign, almost half of which has since been returned by the DNC because of questions about the origin of the funds.
Foreign companies may contribute to presidential campaigns only through U.S. subsidiaries. Contributions by foreign individuals are illegal unless they are U.S. residents.
Huang's attorney has previously been quoted as denying Huang made the proposal to Soberano last summer.
